applicability.note: The SHAPE is as portable as anything this project holds: every elected office in the United States is created by a statute or a charter, and that instrument — not a canvass — is what says whether the office carries a party. It is also cheap, stable and citable: a canvass answers for ONE election and has to be re-read every cycle, while the statute answers for the office until the legislature changes it. Proved on A.R.S. 48-3708 and 48-3709 for the Central Arizona Water Conservation District, where four election-authority documents had failed to settle the same question. The limits are real and worth stating: a statute says what MUST happen and never what DID, so it can establish partisanship, apportionment and term but can never establish that a particular contest appeared on a particular ballot or who filed for it.

routes.title: an expiring term is a POSITION TO BE FILLED and never a ballot contest — check the county board's cancellation resolution before recording either a contest or an absence

applicability.note: A.R.S. 16-410 lets a county board of supervisors cancel any Title 15 or Title 48 district election where the people who filed are fewer than or equal to the positions, appoint them 'fully vested ... as if elected', and forbids the cancelled election from appearing on ANY ballot. So a seat can turn over on schedule while its contest exists in no ballot, no sample ballot and no canvass. THE SHAPE TRAVELS EVEN WHERE THE SECTION NUMBER DOES NOT: uncontested-election cancellation is common across states for school and special districts, and it is the standing explanation for the puzzle 'a term expires this year and we can find no contest'. Do not read that silence as our own retrieval failing, and do not read it as the government failing to hold an election. Read the county's own cancellation resolution. THE COROLLARY THAT BITES: an ABSENCE may not be recorded either, because a true absence now requires knowing an election was cancelled rather than merely not finding one.

outcomes.note: Reconciled the CAWCD 2020 disagreement and DISPROVED the standing inference on NH244 that four expiring Pima seats are therefore four 2026 ballot contests. routes.title: the agenda-vendor portal a district links its board agendas to — and the blanket robots disallow that governs BOTH of the big ones

applicability.note: THE SHAPE IS GENERAL AND IT IS A PERMISSION FACT, NOT A WALL. Two vendor hosts were read on 2026-08-27 and both publish a blanket disallow for every automated client: vailschooldistrict.community.highbond.com/robots.txt (23,479 bytes, 486 User-agent blocks, EXACTLY ONE 'User-agent: *' block carrying 'Disallow: /', and ZERO 'Allow:' directives anywhere in the file) and go.boarddocs.com/robots.txt (21,760 bytes, 'User-agent: * / Disallow: / / Crawl-delay: 1000'). Both were fetched successfully at rung 2, twice, with a bare curl client and with a browser user agent, so this is a READ RULE and not a transport failure — the CANNOT_TELL case of RULING 182 does not apply and must not be claimed here. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY DISTRICT ON THESE PLATFORMS: there is no permitted machine route to the agenda through the vendor, and no number of client variations changes that, because varying the client to defeat a rule is not hunting, it is circumvention. The fact remains owed and the branches that stay eligible are the body's OWN publication, the statutory posting, a different vendor the same body also uses, and a public-records request. routes.title: an ASP.NET search whose hidden date fields are OUTPUTS of a dropdown — why setting them and pressing Search returns the server's own defaults

applicability.note: THE GENERAL SHAPE, AND IT EXPLAINS A WHOLE CLASS OF 'THE PORTAL IGNORED MY QUERY'. On NovusAGENDA's MeetingsResponsive.aspx the visible date inputs txtCalendarFrom and txtCalendarTo carry the DISABLED attribute, and the hidden hfFromDate/hfToDate beside them are written by the ddlDateRange <select> ('Last Month', 'Last Year', 'Custom Date Range', ...). A POST that sets the hidden fields and submits btnSearch therefore sets a value the server recomputes from the dropdown before the search runs, and the response echoes the DEFAULT window rather than the requested one. THE DIAGNOSTIC IS THE ECHO: read back whatever the page reports the applied window to be, and compare it to the window you asked for. Equal means the query ran; different means it did not, and a zero-row result from a query that did not run is a FAILED extraction (RULING 100) and never an absence. THE FIX IS TO OPERATE THE CONTROL THAT OWNS THE VALUE: select the named window, or select 'Custom Date Range' — which is what ENABLES the text boxes — and then type into them. A browser at rung 6 finds this in one step because it refuses to click a disabled element and says so; a hand-built POST cannot find it at all, because a disabled input is still serialisable and still ignored.

routes.title: the instrument check that has to happen before a zero-row result is written down as anything at all

applicability.note: A ZERO IS A CLAIM ABOUT A GOVERNMENT AND AN INSTRUMENT AT THE SAME TIME, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS USUALLY CHECKED. A selector that matches nothing, a table id that changed, a grid that renders after the read — each returns zero, and each reads identically to a body that publishes nothing. THE CHECK IS TO MAKE THE SAME READER RETURN NON-ZERO, in the same session, against something it should find: a wider window, an older year, a sibling tenant, a different body on the same platform. Only after it does is the zero evidence. THE CHECK ITSELF CAN FAIL TO PROVE ANYTHING and that has to be reported rather than absorbed: five candidate Novus tenants were tried on 2026-08-28 as controls and every one was a wildcard error page with no form, which is not a passing control and is not a failing one either. Recording 'the control proved nothing, so the zero proves nothing' is the honest outcome, and it is what keeps a broken reader from being written into the record as a government's silence.

routes.title: an executive's OWN office as the primary source for what they have DONE — a paginated order index whose detail pages carry the date and the signed document

applicability.note: THE RECORD CLASS A CORPUS OF OFFICEHOLDERS USUALLY LACKS. Rosters answer who someone IS; almost nothing answers what they have DONE, and a question about an official's year is unanswerable without it. WHAT WORKS: the office's own site publishes /executive-orders as a paginated index, and each entry links a detail page carrying the designation ('Executive Order 2026-02'), the office's own title for it, the DATE on the line immediately after the designation, the full operative text, and a signed PDF at a predictable path (/sites/default/files/executive-order-<n>.pdf). Walked on azgovernor.gov 2026-08-28: 37 orders indexed across 4 index pages, 12 detail pages read, and 12 of 12 carried BOTH a date and a signed PDF. THE DATE IS THE POINT AND IT IS READ POSITIONALLY AND THEN VALIDATED: 'in the last 12 months' is a window, an order with no date can be placed neither inside nor outside it, and a positional read that is not shape-checked produces a WRONG date the first time the template moves rather than a null. PERMISSION: robots.txt allows every content path with Crawl-delay 10, and the delay is honoured — a public body asking for ten seconds gets ten seconds. THE PORTABILITY CLAIM IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: this is one office on one Drupal template. What travels is the QUESTION — does this officeholder's own office publish its actions with dates and documents? — and that is worth asking of every executive before any third-party aggregator, because the office's own publication is the primary source and an aggregator is a copy of it.

outcomes.note: 12 executive orders with dates and signed PDFs, 6 of them inside the trailing 12 months. Committed to data/officials/az-governor-actions.json with its denominator.

routes.title: bills signed and vetoed — published by the LEGISLATURE rather than the executive, and behind a blanket robots disallow

applicability.note: A GOVERNOR'S RECORD HAS TWO HALVES AND THEY HAVE DIFFERENT PUBLISHERS. Executive orders come from the executive's own office and are readable. Bills signed and vetoed are legislative history, and in Arizona they live in the legislature's bill-status application at apps.azleg.gov, whose robots.txt is 29 bytes: 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'. Read 2026-08-28. That is a PERMISSION verdict and not a wall — no client variation changes it, and varying the client to defeat a published rule is circumvention rather than hunting (RULING 148: a disallow is never re-walked on a clock). WHAT REMAINS ELIGIBLE: www.azleg.gov is ALLOWED with Crawl-delay 120 and named disallows (/DocumentsForBill.asp, /FormatDocument.asp, /ExecutiveNominationsByNominee.asp, /search/), so the legacy site is a live branch that was NOT walked here and is recorded so the next session starts from the permission rather than from a guess. The other eligible branches are the executive office's own announcements of bill action, the Secretary of State's chaptered-laws publication, and a public-records request. Six executive orders presented without saying vetoes are absent reads as a complete account of a governor's year, which is an absence asserted by omission.

applicability.note: THE SHAPE, AND IT IS A PUBLISHING PRACTICE RATHER THAN A DEFECT. Pima County's Legistar tenant answered a 2026-08-01 to 2026-11-01 query with seven events, newest 2026-08-25 and none in September, from an adapter whose forward horizon is 60 days and whose denominators reconcile exactly (fetched 16, normalized 16, three placeless drops accounted). THE DIAGNOSTIC: when a tenant's calendar stops a fortnight out, ask the body's OWN site for a meeting-schedule page before concluding anything about the body; the two records have different publication clocks and a vendor calendar running dry is not a body that has stopped meeting. THE CONTROL that makes this practice rather than code: Vail Unified, same snapshot and same pipeline on the same day, DOES publish individual future sittings and its September 8 and September 22 render. WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE: computing meetings from the rule. Cancellations, holidays and special sessions override a recurring schedule, and rendering a computed date as a published sitting is a render default manufacturing a claim. The rule is a different RECORD, honestly describable as one.

routes.title: the denominator read that decides whether a 'missing rows' report is about the pipeline or about the publisher

applicability.note: A READER SAYING 'THE MEETINGS ARE MISSING' IS A CLAIM ABOUT A SURFACE, AND IT HAS TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT CAUSES THAT LOOK IDENTICAL. Either rows are being lost between the source and the screen, or the source never had them. THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATOR RUNS FIRST AND IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN: the snapshot records fetched, normalized and drops-by-reason per source. If fetched equals normalized and the drops are accounted, no row was lost and the pipeline is not the suspect — which is a strictly stronger statement than 'the code looks right'. THEN ASK THE PRIMARY SOURCE THE SAME QUESTION THE ADAPTER ASKED, by hand, over the same window: if the API returns what the snapshot holds, the adapter is exonerated by observation rather than by inspection. Only then is the question about the publisher, and only then is it worth hunting other routes. Doing this in the other order costs a session: it is possible to read an adapter for an hour and learn nothing that one query would have settled. NOTE THE TRAP IN THE OTHER DIRECTION TOO — a reconciled denominator that is missing required source records is still a wrong result (RULING 100). Reconciling proves nothing was DROPPED; it never proves enough was ASKED FOR.

routes.title: the blocked application and the permitted publisher are two hosts, and only one of them was ever asked

A body very often runs a locked-down interactive app beside an open publication site, and the second one is where the primary documents actually live. routes.title: a stale sitemap on a live site, and the error page that carries the current map

applicability.note: A 404 FROM A PUBLISHED SITEMAP IS A LEAD AND NOT A WALL. www.azleg.gov advertises robotsitemap.xml; it lists 28 .asp URLs written against a scheme the site has since left, and SessionLaws.asp returns HTTP 404. Most walks stop there and record the route as dead. Reading the hrefs off the error page produced the two routes the walk was looking for, both at new addresses. THE RULE: when a URL from a sitemap, an old bookmark or a search result 404s on a host that is otherwise up, EXTRACT THE LINKS FROM THE ERROR RESPONSE before concluding anything. Check the status AND the body — a 404 with 78 KB of navigation is a redirect nobody wrote, and the site is telling you where everything went on the page that says the old address is gone. The same shape appears wherever a body migrates CMS, which they all eventually do.

So when an executive's own site is thin or the bill-status application is walled, ASK THE RECEIVING BODY FOR THE SAME ACT — a legislature that receives the governor's letters publishes them. The same reasoning reaches session laws, journals and enrolled-bill lists, all of which are records of one act held by more than one government.
